column6: Core Idea called a.s. "the strongest form of convergence"; it does not imply L^p convergence. Reworded to "a strong form (it implies convergence in probability)".
Clarity only: bullet 2 cited "posterior mean 8/12" with no prior or data; added "With a Beta(1, 1) prior and 7 heads in 10 flips".
Old Core Idea uses banned word "crucial"; left (out of scope).

Tower bullet said "It needs one inside the other"; overstated (identity can hold for non-nested sigma-algebras, e.g. X G1-measurable and G1, G2 independent). Now "The general identity needs one inside the other."
Old Core Idea "Shortest confidence intervals use the critical region from the UMP test" is loose (UMP inversion gives UMA sets); not changed.
Explainer said L^p convergence is "weaker than almost sure convergence", contradicted by its own typewriter example; now "neither implies the other".
Explainer sat before Questions; moved after Questions (text otherwise unchanged).
Core Idea said equality holds iff T is the UMVUE; false (a UMVUE need not attain the bound) and contradicted the Explainer (equality iff T is linear in the score). Reworded.
Old Core Idea defines spectral gap as "largest minus second-largest eigenvalue"; loose (usually 1 − second-largest modulus); not changed.
Used s² in the Gamma estimates while the Misconceptions say MoM uses the divisor-n variance; replaced with σ̂² defined as the divisor-n sample variance (numbers unchanged).
Clarity only: "The n − 1 version is a later correction" could read as history (Bessel's correction predates Pearson's method); now "a separate bias correction".
Uniqueness needs the MGF to be finite near 0 states a sufficient condition as necessary (e.g. Carleman's condition is weaker); now "A sufficient condition is...".
